title: Flock device inventory and purchases since February 2026
summary:
Temporal follow-up to the February 2026 device-list production under W012201-022326. Asks for:

- Item 1: devices installed, activated, replaced, relocated, decommissioned, or taken offline since 2026-02-01, with location (prior and new, for relocations), device type/model, ALPR capability, date of change, and records documenting the reason.
- Item 2: invoices, purchase orders, order forms, quotes, and contract amendments with Flock Safety dated on or after 2026-02-01, including installation fees or charges beyond the MSA and Amendment No. 1.
- Item 3: the current full device list — location, model designation (Falcon, Condor, Picard, or other), ALPR capability, ownership status (SMPD-owned, community camera, or other), and installation date.
- Item 4: communications with Flock Safety since 2026-02-01 requesting additions, removals, or corrections to the device information shown on the transparency portal, and records of when those changes were completed.

On 2026-08-20 the City produced item 2 and stated items 1, 3, and 4 are still being processed. Two records were produced:

- Flock invoice INV-90909, dated 2026-04-01, $45,000.00, annotated "CA - San Mateo PD (ORC): Year 3 of 36 Month Term, 2026 - 2027" — 13 × "Flock Safety LPR, fka Falcon" and 2 × "Flock Safety Video Camera PTZ w/ LTE Service, fka Condor" at $3,000.00 each. Contracted billing structure 50%/25%/25%; PO# field blank.
- City purchase order PO-0001983, dated 2026-04-27, $45,000.00, comment "2026 Flock Safety ORT" — same 15 line-item devices, issued 26 days after the invoice it pays.

policy_promises.quote: implement a usage and privacy policy ... that includes the location of the ALPR system
policy_promises.tests: Whether the Department maintains a current, complete device inventory distinguishing ALPR-capable devices from non-ALPR cameras.
What purchase and amendment records exist for device changes made outside the MSA and Amendment No. 1.

prior_pra_refs.note: Produced the 2026-02-26 device list; item 3 asks for the current list in the same form.

Produced the 2024 ORT grant procurement records — Amendment No. 1 order form, the 2024-03-18 Council Agenda Report and Resolution No. 21 (2024), and Purchase Order PO-0001042 ($48,950). PO-0001983 produced here is the 2026 continuation of that ORT-funded purchase.

filed_because: The February 2026 device list is the last full inventory on the record. Item 4 tests the Department's February statement that two decommissioned devices would be deducted from the transparency site and that cameras marked "in planning" were rejected locations Flock was working to remove — asking what was actually communicated to Flock and when the changes were completed.
notes:
Filed 2026-08-16; 10-day statutory determination due 2026-08-26.

Partial production 2026-08-20: item 2 produced (INV-90909 and PO-0001983); items 1, 3, and 4 stated to be still in processing, with no date given.

These 15 devices are not a new purchase. Amendment No. 1 (effective 2024-03-04, produced under W012459-040226) bought "fifteen (15) additional automated license plate reader devices for a three-year term"; its Exhibit C order form lists 13 Falcon + 2 Condor PTZ w/ LTE + FlockOS at $45,000.00 annual recurring over a 36-month initial term. INV-90909 is the Year 3 annual-recurring payment on that same Exhibit C — identical 13 + 2 composition, identical $45,000.00 total. The devices sit inside the existing fleet, not on top of it: the Flock portal camera_count went 68 (2026-02-18) to 66 (2026-03-12) and stayed at 66 through 2026-08-13, unchanged across both the 2026-04-01 invoice and the 2026-04-27 PO.

Open questions the unproduced items 1, 3, and 4 would resolve:

- Amendment No. 1's recital and PO-0001042 both describe the buy as 15 ALPR devices, but Exhibit C is 13 ALPR + 2 Condor PTZ video cameras — the plate-reader count is overstated by two in the contract recital and the purchase order.
- Exhibit C's billing schedule placed the Year 3 $45,000.00 annual recurring at 2025-04-01. The Year 3 invoice produced here is dated 2026-04-01 and annotated "2026 - 2027". Item 2'\''s 2026-02-01 cutoff means any 2025-04-01 invoice would not have been responsive, so the record here cannot show whether the schedule slipped a year or a year was billed twice.
- PO-0001983 (2026-04-27) postdates by 26 days the invoice it pays (2026-04-01), and the invoice'\''s PO# field is blank. The 2024 cycle ran the same way (PO-0001042 dated 2024-04-11).
- Camera #50 "(ORT Grant)", shown decommissioned 2025-10-21 in the February 2026 location spreadsheet, was relocated rather than removed: the Camera Manager export lists it live at E/B Hillsdale Bl @ Campus Dr (serial 250228Q021003CH, 100% uptime), while the E/B Hillsdale Bl @ Countryside Dr row is a placeholder with Serial "-". The strikethrough rows mark retired *locations*, not retired devices, so the 13-Falcon billing is consistent.

Parser derived '\''needs_review'\'' because the 2026-08-20 partial production names no date for the remaining items; status set manually to rolling_production.

Device-count context from the February 2026 Camera Manager export (W012201-022326), which is image-only; counts below are from its OCR sidecar and the record images:

- The export header reads "80 Total Devices" / "Live Locations (80)". Exact-line label counts: 66 "LPR Camera" records and 15 "Picard" records.
- 13 records carry Serial "-" with source "Salesforce": eight "In Planning" (#02-#09, the Hillsdale / 31st Ave / Sailer / Edison / El Camino corridor), four retired-location placeholders (30, 33, 50, 53), and one rejected Picard (P#001 Franklin Pkwy West @ Whole Foods Market - REJECTED).
- Twelve of those 13 sit inside the 66 "LPR Camera" records, leaving 54 LPR records with actual hardware serials.
- The Flock portal camera_count has read 66 since 2026-03-12, matching the count of LPR Camera *records* rather than the count of serialized devices. UNVERIFIED: the export predates the portal's 68->66 drop, and the portal's counting basis is inferred, not documented. Worth confirming before citing.

Delaware @ Concar, as of the February 2026 export - relevant to any field observation of a southbound camera there:

- 30 - W/B Concar @ Delaware St (Towards W/B Hwy 92) (front plate - E/B traffic), serial 230227200AC, 100% uptime - live, sited on Concar.
- 32 - N/B Delaware @ Concar Dr (Towards Post Office/16th Ave), serial 241012Q02100F35, 96% uptime, last visited 2024-08-08 - live, northbound on Delaware.
- P#006 Delaware @ Concar Dr, serial 250905P021010DB, and C#006 Delaware @ Concar Dr.
- "30 - Out of Service (Relocation to S/B Delaware @ Concar) - Original", Serial "-", status Decommissioned.

Field observation 2026-08-20 confirms three ALPR at this intersection: one on Concar approaching the W/B Hwy 92 onramp, and two on Delaware at Concar, one facing north and one facing south. The Concar unit matches live record 30 and the northbound Delaware unit matches live record 32, but no serialized record corresponds to the southbound Delaware unit - it appears only inside the decommissioned placeholder, and the location spreadsheet's numbered list gives it no row.

Because the Concar camera is still physically present, record 30 cannot be a stale location name for the southbound Delaware device; they are separate units. Serial prefixes across the export are consistent with a YYMM manufacture date (all fall between 2109 and 2511), which would place record 30's 230227200AC at 2023-02 - old hardware, matching the Concar camera's long presence. That reading is inference, not documented, and record 32 sits awkwardly with it (serial 241012Q02100F35 against a "last visited 2024-08-08"), so it should not be relied on.

Item 1 remains the lever: a deployed, field-verifiable ALPR at southbound Delaware @ Concar is absent from the February 2026 inventory.
